overall_summary: Bitcoin faces near-term pressure from record IBIT outflows, surging real yields, a strong dollar, and hawkish Fed signals that keep rate-cut hopes distant. Institutional accumulation remains a longer-term positive, and a few geopolitical de-escalation notes offer limited relief, but the immediate macro and flow backdrop stays heavy. Crypto is likely to stay range-bound to softer until yields and dollar strength ease.
key_points: Record IBIT outflow and yields weigh on BTC
Fed hawks and strong dollar keep pressure on
Q3 institutional BTC adds are supportive longer-term
MoonPay bank-charter bid is crypto-infrastructure positive
Mixed geopolitics: strikes vs. delayed Iran and peace talk

items.title: BlackRock IBIT Sees Record $541M Outflow as BTC Slides
items.summary: BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust posted a record single-day net outflow of five hundred forty-one million dollars on Thursday, the biggest since launch, driving total US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows to about five hundred eighty-two million. Bitcoin fell to nearly sixty-one thousand two hundred before recovering above sixty-one thousand seven hundred, down for a third straight day, as the tech selloff after Anthropic's IPO spread to Asia and US futures. Liquidations hit roughly seven hundred nineteen million dollars in twenty-four hours, with the vast majority long positions forced out, and open interest declined as traders de-levered. Traders should watch whether outflows persist and if the sixty-one thousand support holds, because sustained ETF selling plus long flushes often extend downside in risk-off tape.
items.impact: Near-term selling pressure and de-leveraging risk while ETF redemptions stay heavy

items.title: Surging Real Yields Crash Gold and Weigh on Bitcoin
items.summary: Gold dropped to its lowest since September twenty twenty-five as US two-year real yields pushed above two point four percent and longer real rates hit multi-decade highs, making non-yielding assets less attractive. The same real-rate shock is cited as a key headwind for Bitcoin, which has slid alongside precious metals and tech. Higher risk-free returns compete directly with crypto and gold for capital, especially with Fed hike talk still alive. Traders should care because this macro backdrop can keep pressure on BTC even if crypto-specific news turns quieter.
items.impact: Macro headwind that can prolong risk-off selling across BTC and gold

items.title: Institutions Net-Add 49k BTC in Q3, Holdings Hit Record
items.summary: Galaxy Research analysis of thirteen-F filings shows institutional managers added a net forty-nine thousand two hundred twenty-nine Bitcoin equivalent to US spot Bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, reversing three straight quarters of net selling. Reported holdings reached a record three hundred fifty-six thousand four hundred ninety-one BTC, worth nearly thirty billion at quarter-end prices, with Wells Fargo becoming the largest single holder after a big add. Wealth platforms and advisors drove much of the buying. Even though this is lagging data while current daily flows are negative, it signals structural institutional demand that can matter once the short-term risk-off fades.
items.impact: Supports longer-term bid from traditional finance despite recent daily outflows

items.title: MoonPay Files for OCC National Trust Bank Charter
items.summary: Crypto payments firm MoonPay has applied to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to form MoonPay National Trust Bank, a non-depository national trust bank focused on digital-asset custody, stablecoin issuance and redemption, reserve management, and conversion services. The filing comes ahead of the GENIUS Act framework for payment stablecoins taking effect in January twenty twenty-seven. Approval would give MoonPay a single federal umbrella for these activities and put it in the same regulatory lane as other crypto firms seeking trust bank status. Traders should note this as further institutionalization of stablecoin and custody infrastructure, which tends to be constructive for market plumbing and confidence.
items.impact: Positive regulatory step for stablecoin and custody rails if approved

items.title: CFTC: No Special Rules for Hyperliquid Onchain Venues
items.summary: CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said onchain platforms such as Hyperliquid that want to offer derivatives to US retail traders must either register as an exchange or partner with an already registered one, and will face the same requirements as traditional venues. There will be no lighter touch just because the tech is onchain. He pointed to Backpack's recent US licenses as a workable path. This gives clearer rules of the road for bringing perp and onchain derivatives onshore but also confirms compliance costs and barriers remain high, so traders should treat it as regulatory clarity rather than an immediate green light for unrestricted access.
items.impact: Clarity on US path for onchain perps without opening floodgates

items.title: VanEck Ends Gemini Custody for BTC ETH SOL ETFs
items.summary: VanEck is terminating Gemini's custody and clearing agreements for its US Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana ETFs, with the changes effective around mid-February twenty twenty-seven. Coinbase Custody will remain and become the continuing custodian across the three funds; the Solana ETF's Gemini staking addendum also ends. No reason was given in the SEC filings. This is operational rather than directional news, but it concentrates more ETF custody with Coinbase and removes a major mandate from Gemini, so watch for any follow-on comments on staking continuity or competitive shifts in institutional custody.
items.impact: Custody consolidation toward Coinbase; limited immediate price effect

items.title: Fed Officials Signal More Hikes, Open to 50bp December Move
items.summary: FOMC minutes and fresh comments from Waller, Paulson, and Goolsbee show almost all policymakers see further rate increases as needed to fight sticky inflation above target. Waller has floated a half-point hike next month to shock markets if needed, while Goolsbee left all options on the table including larger moves amid AI-driven demand risks. Traders should care because this locks in a December hike and raises the odds of a steeper path, tightening financial conditions.
items.impact: Higher rates and reduced liquidity pressure risk assets including Bitcoin

items.title: US Dollar Index Holds Near 19-Month Highs
items.summary: The DXY sits around 103.8, close to its strongest level since April 2025, on track for a fourth weekly gain. Strength comes from firm rate-hike bets and safe-haven flows as AI-related equities wobble. Crypto traders watch this closely because a stronger dollar often coincides with weaker Bitcoin and risk assets as global liquidity tightens.
items.impact: Dollar strength typically weighs on crypto prices

items.title: Michigan Consumer Sentiment Rises to 51, Inflation Expectations Ease
items.summary: The final University of Michigan reading for November came in at 51, up from 48 in October, with year-ahead inflation expectations dropping to 4.3 percent and longer-term to 3.4 percent. Gains were driven by independents and lower-wealth households even as stock owners stayed cautious amid AI worries. This soft data offers a mild positive for growth but the still-elevated inflation views keep the Fed focused on tightening.
items.impact: Slightly supportive for risk assets if it softens rate path, but inflation still hot

items.title: Jobless Claims Edge Higher, Continuing Claims Jump
items.summary: Initial claims rose to 203,000 last week, a touch above the 198,000 forecast, while continuing claims climbed 70,000 to 1.763 million. The labor market stays low-fire overall but some workers are taking longer to find new jobs. Crypto traders note this mixed signal leaves the Fed room to prioritize inflation over employment fears for now.
items.impact: Keeps Fed hawkish bias intact without signaling recession

items.title: Philly Fed Manufacturing Slumps to Six-Month Low
items.summary: The Philadelphia Fed general activity index dropped sharply to 6.3 in November from 20.9, missing expectations near 20, with new orders turning negative. Prices paid jumped to 58.2, the highest since April, showing cooling activity alongside sticky cost pressures. This points to softer growth that could eventually ease inflation but currently reinforces the need for restrictive policy.
items.impact: Weaker manufacturing data mixed with hot prices supports higher-for-longer rates

items.title: Treasury Yields Dip on Safe-Haven Demand Amid Equity Weakness
items.summary: The 10-year yield fell toward 5 percent or below on Friday as investors sought bonds during an AI-driven stock selloff, even as shorter yields stay elevated on hike expectations. Markets still price nearly full odds of a 25-basis-point December increase. For traders this relief in yields is temporary if Fed speakers keep the hawkish drumbeat going later today.
items.impact: Lower yields offer short-term support but rate path remains the bigger driver

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin Hold First Trilateral Summit in Shenzhen
items.summary: US President Trump, China's Xi and Russia's Putin met for the first time as a trio in Shenzhen and issued a joint declaration calling for more oil supplies, lower nuclear risks and UN reform. The statement skipped any concrete deals on the Ukraine or Iran wars. Traders should watch this because the oil-supply pledge and any de-escalation signal can swing energy prices and overall risk appetite for Bitcoin and equities.
items.impact: Mixed oil/risk signal; limited concrete progress keeps uncertainty high

items.title: Russia Hits Three Kyiv Bridges in Major Missile Barrage
items.summary: Overnight Russian ballistic missiles and drones struck three key bridges across the Dnipro in Kyiv, killing several people, cutting power and snarling the capital after Putin vowed retaliation for Ukraine's hits on the Crimean Bridge. This is one of the biggest infrastructure attacks on the capital in the war. Escalation raises energy and risk-off pressure just as peace talk rumors circulate, so crypto traders need to track whether it derails diplomacy or fuels more volatility.
items.impact: Heightens war risk premium and potential risk-off flows

items.title: Houthis Strike Riyadh's Tallest Tower, PIF Headquarters
items.summary: Iran-backed Houthis hit the Public Investment Fund Tower, Riyadh's tallest skyscraper and Saudi sovereign wealth fund HQ, damaging multiple floors with no reported injuries. It follows a recent Aramco tower strike and comes amid wider Red Sea and Gulf tensions. This keeps a geopolitical risk premium in oil and can spill into broader risk assets if Saudi or regional responses escalate.
items.impact: Supports oil risk premium and Middle East volatility

items.title: Trump Delays Fresh Iran Strike Decision Until 2027
items.summary: President Trump said he is not rushing any decision on renewed major strikes against Iran and will wait until after the start of 2027, even as skirmishes and tanker attacks continue in the Strait of Hormuz. The US maintains its naval blockade. Pushing the decision out reduces the chance of an immediate big escalation, which could ease short-term oil spikes and support risk assets if markets read it as cooler heads prevailing.
items.impact: Lowers near-term escalation risk for oil and risk markets

items.title: Kushner: Russia Open to NATO-Style Ukraine Guarantees
items.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner told European and Ukrainian leaders in Berlin that Russia appears comfortable with Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine as part of a broader package. German Chancellor Merz said four-way talks involving Ukraine, Russia, the US and Europe could come soon, possibly in a neutral venue. Any credible path to de-escalation would be a major risk-on catalyst for markets and crypto after years of war.
items.impact: Potential de-risking if talks advance; still highly conditional

items.title: Oil Edges Lower Despite Hormuz Attacks and Houthi Strikes
items.summary: Crude prices fell Friday and headed for a third weekly drop as Middle East export flows recovered near pre-war levels, even after Houthi hits on Riyadh and reports of tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. IEA warnings and OPEC+ meetings loom. Soft oil on supply recovery can ease inflation pressure and support risk assets, but lingering attack risks mean sudden spikes remain possible.
items.impact: Supply recovery weighs on oil; geopolitics still a volatility driver
